page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre above the text. Page number top right. Text in one column of short verse lines: first a French stanza continuing from the previous page, then a heading "LAT." with a Latin stanza, then a rule, a heading "XIX. GAL." with a French stanza, then "LAT." with a Latin stanza. Signature at bottom right. No margin notes.

main_text.p:
Dessus vne boule ronde:
Flotant au milieu de l'onde.
main_text.head: LAT.

p.i:
SECVRA si quis spe vagus ocia
Fallacis aui carpere cogitat:
Si rebus illis nititur, quas
Sorte videt variare caca:
Nixus vagantis remigio globi
Quem fluctus vnda, quem rotat impetus
Venti furentis: se per omne
Incolumem fore credit æquor.

main_text.head: XIX. GAL.
main_text.p:
IAMAIS n'auoir, & toufiours defirer,
Sont les effects de qui aime le Monde.
Plus en honneu & richefles abonde,
Et plus encor on l'y void aspirer.
Il ne icuit de cela qui eft fien:
Il veut l'autrui, il l'eftime, il l'adore.
Quand il a tout, c'eft alors qu'il n'a rien:
Car ayant tout, to at il defire encore.
main_text.head: LAT.

p.i:
QVEMCVNQVE Mundi cæcus amor rapit
Illum cupido torquet inefficax,
Si dentur ingentes auaro

page.notes: Lines transcribed as printed; the first French stanza may continue from the previous page. Several letters in the French are damaged or faint (e.g. "icuit", "to at", "eftime") and were copied as they appear; "Mundi cæcus" is set in a large italic initial "M". The Latin "SECVRA" and "QVEMCVNQVE" show large initial capitals. The rule above "XIX." is a horizontal printed line, not text. The last Latin line ends the page with the running text continuing on the next page.
